market_holds: Spot $4.005 at the 2026-11-18 close (sealed baseline): 5-day run-up -4.2%, 20-day +1.7%, 36.8% below the 52-week high and 10.6% above the low, 20-day realised vol 55.8%. There is no options market, so no implied move. The usual move from Yahoo daily bars (own arithmetic) is about 9-12% on the close of print day: Nov-2024 +13.8%, Mar-2025 +9.4%, Aug-2025 -1.7%, Nov-2025 opened +9.2% and closed +1.0%, Mar-11-2026 -10.1% (after +11.7% the day before), May-19-2026 +11.6% (then -9.8% the next day), Aug-20-2026 -11.1% (opened -8.5%). The stock is roughly flat since the August print ($4.08 close on 2026-08-20). Consensus (Earnings Whispers preview of 2026-11-11, via finviz) is Q3 revenue $944.0M, about RMB6.34B, which is the LOW end of the company's RMB6.34-6.44B guide and down from about $969M before the guide. Consensus EPS is $0.10 against $0.05 a year ago. The guide was 23.1-25.1% y/y growth on Q3-2025's RMB5,149.2M, flat to down quarter on quarter from Q2's RMB6.61B. The stock trades on the next-quarter revenue guide: Q2 beat the top of its range by 4.3% and fell 11% on the softer Q3 guide. Short interest is unknown.
view: ATRenew sets conservative revenue guides and has beaten the top of its range in each of the last three quarters: Q4-25 by 1.2%, Q1-26 by 3.4%, Q2-26 by 4.3% (own arithmetic). A comparable Q3 lands at about RMB6.5-6.7B, 26-30% y/y, about 3-5% above a consensus that sits at the bottom of the guide. The sales bar is therefore low, but anyone who knows the pattern expects that beat, so it is not where the reaction is decided. The line is the Q4 guide against Q4-25's RMB6,254M, plus margins against a consensus EPS that implies doubling. Since the company last spoke, independent data is mixed. Positive: Apple's Greater China revenue rose 21% in the September quarter, with iPhone up strong double digits, and the iPhone 18 Pro went on sale 2026-09-18, so high-value iPhone trade-in supply flows into Q4. Memory-driven price rises on new phones are lifting used-phone prices (Zhuanzhuan's average used-phone selling price is up 8-10% over ten months), a driver management itself cited. The national 15% phone subsidy runs to 2026-12-31 with all four tranches released by about 2026-09-30. Negative: China smartphone shipments fell 10-15% y/y in Q3 (IDC -15.4%, Counterpoint -10%, Omdia -12%), Counterpoint expects the pressure to continue into Q4, and Android trade-in supply follows new-unit sales. Service revenue fell for the first time in Q2 on merchant fee cuts. Recycling-quote complaints were in the press on 2026-11-12. The last four prints alternated about ±10% on the guide, often with a sharp fade or reversal within a day, and the pre-print tape is neutral. On balance the setup leans slightly up: expectations are reset, the stock is near its lows, and Apple and used-phone pricing are tailwinds. But the Q4 guide could just as easily read as another deceleration, so I cannot see a direction the price has missed with any confidence.
unpriced: Possibly the strength of Apple's China sell-through and the rise in used-phone selling prices since August, which consensus does not visibly carry: revenue consensus sits at the low end of the guide and was cut after it. That is only a revenue-beat argument, and the reaction is decided by the Q4 guide, which these data do not pin down. So nothing is shown to be unpriced at a size worth betting on.

recommendation.reason: The Q3 revenue beat is near certain on the company's pattern and the bar is low, but the reaction has turned on the next-quarter guide every time. Independent data on Q4 conflict: Apple China strength and higher used-phone prices on one side, a 10-15% fall in China smartphone shipments with Counterpoint expecting more weakness on the other. My edge on the sign of the guide surprise is well under the 65% the playbook requires.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: A Q4 revenue guide at or above about 25% y/y (RMB7.8B or more on the RMB6,254M base), together with a Q3 non-GAAP operating margin above Q2's 3.1%, would make a long reasonable. A guide near or below 20% would make the down case.

self_critique: The case for a clear long: consensus is stale at the guide low end, the stock is near its 52-week low having de-rated on one guide, and Apple's +21% China quarter with the iPhone 18 Pro launch in late September points straight at stronger Q4 trade-in supply and higher used-phone prices, so a Q4 guide in the mid-20s is plausible and could pop a de-rated stock. The case for a short: China phone shipments are at a 14-year low and still weakening, the Q3 guide already implied a q/q decline, and EPS consensus requires a doubling. A second soft guide would confirm the deceleration story, and this stock's history is sharp moves on the guide. Neither case is strong enough to clear 65%.
approach_notes: Finding the line first (the next-quarter guide) and checking the freshest counterparty data (IDC, Apple China) was what helped, along with own arithmetic on the beat pattern versus consensus. The [P4] framing would have pushed toward 'consensus is stale, so buy', but the stale number is revenue and the stock trades on the guide, so it had to be resisted.
